lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Saturday, **14 March**, eight a.m. Her school hall.
**Mr Tan:** Kavya! **14 March**: **3.14**! **Pi Day!** Eleven months I've planned this fair.
**Kavya:** Mr Tan, it's a Saturday. Why am I here?
**Mr Tan:** Every visitor gets a **Pi Passport**. Every right answer gets my stamp: **EASY AS PI**.
**Dad:** Dad's **Pi-zza**, reporting for duty! I've rounded π to **3**. Close enough!
**Mr Tan:** And wrong answers get **HALF-BAKED**.
**Ah Boy:** Who's that man? He's been talking since the car park.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is about the guest of honour. He arrived at seven. He hasn't stopped talking.
**Uncle Pi:** **Uncle Pi!** Kavya! We met at your family photo. I'm still on the same sentence.
**Ah Boy:** When does he stop?
**Mr Tan:** He doesn't. He's **irrational**. His digits **never end** and **never repeat**.
**Uncle Pi:** Today, every **circle** in this school is mine! …**32384626**…
**Narrator:** Easy as Pi. Episode 16: The Pi Day Fair.
**Narrator:** Nine a.m. The school field. Mr Tan's first stall: **Draw a Giant Circle**.
**Mr Tan:** One peg, one rope, one Priya. Rope tight, Priya. Run!
**Priya:** Done! Fastest circle in Year 8. Do I win?
**Rad:** Hey. Rad. The **radius**. I was the rope. Centre to edge.
**Rad:** Every point on a circle is the **same distance** from the **centre**. That distance is me: **r**.
**Dee:** And I'm **Dee**, his big brother. The **diameter**: edge to edge, **through the centre**. **d = 2r**. Twice the man.
**Priya:** Easy. I drew a line **13 cm** long in a circle of radius **6 cm**.
**Dee:** A line joining two points on the circle is a **chord**. The longest chord is me: 2 × 6 = **12 cm**. Thirteen? Impossible.
**Perry:** Perry. I walk the **circumference**, all the way **around**. Stop part of the way, and that's an **arc**.
**Tan Gent:** Tan Gent. A **tangent**. I touch the circle at **one** point only, at **90°** to the radius. Then I leave.
**Mr Tan:** No relation.
**Mum:** A pizza slice: **two radii** and an **arc**. That's a **sector**.
**Mum:** One straight cut across my cake: the piece a **chord** cuts off is a **segment**.
**Kavya:** **seC**tor reaches the **C**entre. A segment never does.
**Ah Boy:** Small piece: **minor**. Big piece: **major**. I'll take the major.

chapters.title: Measure a circle, win a prize

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Ten a.m. The hall. Uncle Pi's stall: **Measure a circle, win a prize**.
**Kavya:** String once round, ruler straight across. Coin: **7.8 cm** round, **2.5 cm** across.
**Uncle Pi:** Now divide! **Circumference ÷ diameter**, every one. …**43383279**…
**Uncle Pi:** That's me! **π = C ÷ d**. The **same** for every circle, coin or Ferris wheel.
**Mr Tan:** Not all exactly the same? **Measuring errors**: stretchy string, rounded readings.
**Dad:** So π is **22/7**. A nice fraction. Close enough!
**Uncle Pi:** **22/7** = 3.142857 142857… It **repeats**! I **never** repeat. I'm **irrational**.
**Mr Tan:** Calculator: the **π button**. No calculator: **3.14** or **22/7**. **Exact**: leave the **π** in.
**Ah Boy:** If your numbers never end, how does a circle ever **close**?
**Uncle Pi:** …Nobody has ever asked me that.
**Kavya:** The circle closes fine. It's only the **number** that never ends.
**Mr Tan:** Never start a conversation with Uncle Pi. He goes on and on.
**Uncle Pi:** Ho ho! On and on! …**50288419**…
**Narrator:** Eleven a.m. Stall three: **Guess the Roll**. Mr Tan's bicycle.
**Mr Tan:** My wheel: **70 cm** across. One full turn. **More** or **less** than **2 m**?
**Priya:** Less. Obviously. Seventy is tiny.
**Dad:** π is 3, so 3 × 70 = **210 cm**. Close enough!
**Uncle Pi:** One turn rolls out one **circumference**. **C = πd** = π × 70 = **219.9 cm**!
**Mr Tan:** Dad: **10 cm** short. Use the **π button**, and round **once**, at the **end**.
**Ah Boy:** **C**herry **P**ie **D**elicious! **C = πd**!
**Rad:** Only got me? Double me first: **C = 2πr**.
**Mr Tan:** Radius **4.5 cm**: C = 2 × π × 4.5 = **9π cm**. Exact: **in terms of π**.
**Kavya:** Or rounded: 9π = 28.27…, so **28.3 cm** to 1 d.p. Just over 3 × 9. ✓
**Uncle Pi:** The Singapore Flyer: **150 m** across, so one lap is π × 150 ≈ **471 m**. Wheee!
**Mum:** The school pond is **40 m** round. What's its radius?
**Dad:** 40 ÷ π = **12.7 m**. Close enough!
**Dee:** Did somebody say **across**? **C ÷ π** gives **me**, the diameter!
**Kavya:** So cut it in half: **r = C ÷ 2π** = 40 ÷ 2π ≈ **6.4 m**.
**Narrator:** Noon. Dad's Pi-zza. Small, **20 cm** across: **$12**. Large, **30 cm** across: **$24**.
**Priya:** Double the price, double the pizza. Same deal.
**Mr Tan:** Dad, cut one into **8** slices. Ah Boy, line them up: point up, point down.
**Ah Boy:** It's a wobbly rectangle!
**Mr Tan:** Half the crust on top, half below: each long edge is half the circumference, **πr**. The height: **r**.
**Mr Tan:** Thinner slices: a rectangle **πr** by **r**. So **A = πr × r = πr²**.
**Ah Boy:** **A**pple **P**ies **are too**! **A = πr²**!
**Ah Boy:** Small pizza: π × 20² = **1257 cm²**!
**Dee:** Did somebody say **twenty**? That's me!
**Rad:** You used my brother. **D is for Double**: cut him in half first, or the answer is **4 times** too big.
**Dad:** My calculator: π × 10 = 31.4, squared, **987**. Bigger pizza!
**Mr Tan:** That's **(πr)²**. Only **r** is squared: **square** the radius **first**, then × π.
**Kavya:** Large: **r = 15**, A = **225π ≈ 707 cm²**. **2.25 times** the pizza, for **twice** the price.
**Rad:** Double the radius, and the area goes up **4 times**: **π(2r)² = 4πr²**.
**Mr Tan:** Backwards: **r = √(A ÷ π)**. A **450 cm²** pizza: √(450 ÷ π) ≈ **12 cm**, so **24 cm** across.
**Dad:** So the large is the better deal. I knew that. I priced it.
**Narrator:** One p.m. Mum's cake stall. Round cakes, **20 cm** across, sold by the **half** and the **quarter**.
**Mum:** Every half-cake gets a ribbon right round its edge. Priya, cut the ribbon.
**Priya:** A semicircle is half a circle, so: half the circumference! ½ × π × 20 ≈ **31.4 cm**.
**Perry:** Perry. I walked your ribbon. It ends here, at the cut. The **straight edge** is bare!
**Kavya:** **Trace it with your finger**: the curve **plus** the diameter. 31.4 + 20 = **51.4 cm**.
**Mr Tan:** Exact: **10π + 20** cm. They don't combine, just like **10x + 20**.
**Mum:** The top is easier: half the area. ½ × π × 10² = **50π ≈ 157 cm²**.
**Ah Boy:** I'll have a **quarter**! With a quarter of a ribbon!
**Perry:** A quarter circle has **two** straight edges. Two radii. I walk both. My legs.
**Mum:** And the area: ¼ × π × 10² = **25π ≈ 78.5 cm²**.
**Ah Boy:** Can I eat it now?
**Perry:** I'm still walking round it.
**Narrator:** Two p.m. The school track. Priya challenges Dad to one lap.
**Mr Tan:** Two straights, **100 m** each. A **semicircle** at each end. **60 m** across.
**Dad:** Two hundred metres and a bit of curve. Close enough. Go!
**Kavya:** Push the two semicircles together: one **whole circle**, **60 m** across.
**Dad:** …I'll walk.
**Perry:** And I don't cut across the field. **Perimeter**: the **outside** only. Lines **inside** don't count.
**Mr Tan:** The field inside: rectangle **plus** circle. 100 × 60 + π × 30² ≈ **8827 m²**. **Add** the pieces.
**Mum:** The pond has radius **3 m**. The new path round it is **1 m** wide. How much paving?
**Ah Boy:** That path is for ants.
**Perry:** Thank you.
**Kavya:** **Subtract areas**, not radii: π × 4² − π × 3² = 16π − 9π = **7π ≈ 22.0 m²**.
**Mr Tan:** A **ring**: **π(R² − r²)**. Never **π(R − r)²**.
**Narrator:** Three p.m. **Stretch** time. The last pizza: radius **15 cm**, cut into **8** equal slices.
**Sal:** Sal. A **sector**. Two radii and an arc. Every one of us is a **fraction** of a circle.
**Kavya:** Eight tips share **360°**, so each is **45°**. 45/360 = **⅛** of the pizza.
**Sal:** My crust is an **arc**: **θ/360 × 2πr** = ⅛ × 30π ≈ **11.8 cm**.
**Mr Tan:** Eight slices. That's what I call **a pizza the action**.
**Uncle Pi:** Ho ho! A pizza the action! …**71693993**…
**Ah Boy:** I want a bigger slice. **120°**!
**Mr Tan:** 120/360 = **⅓** of the pizza. Area: ⅓ × 225π = **75π ≈ 235.6 cm²**.
**Priya:** His crust: ⅓ × 30π = **10π ≈ 31.4 cm**.
**Perry:** Perimeter? Crust **plus two radii**: 31.4 + 15 + 15 = **61.4 cm**. I walked it. Twice.
**Dad:** Last slice for the guest of honour: **0°**. Close enough?

chapters.title: The fair saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits, the fair would like to save you some marks.
**Dee:** One. The area, **A = πr²**, needs the **radius**. Use me and it's **4 times** too big. **Cut me in half first.**
**Ah Boy:** Two. **Square** the radius **first**, then × π. Not **(πr)²**. Dad's calculator says sorry.
**Perry:** Three. Semicircle, quarter or sector? **Add the straight edges**. My feet thank you.
**Rad:** Four. **C ÷ π** gives the **diameter**. To get me, cut it in half.
**Dad:** Five. Round **once**, at the **end**. π is not 3. Close enough is **not** close enough.
**Mr Tan:** Six. **Area** in **cm²**, length in **cm**. And '**in terms of π**' means **leave the π in**.
**Narrator:** Easy as Pi will return.
**Narrator:** Nine p.m. The hall is empty. Almost.
**Mr Tan:** Uncle Pi, one last one. Why **pi r squared**? Pies are **round**!
**Uncle Pi:** Ho ho ho! Pies are round! …**44592307**…
